charts.title: One Tesla V100 32 GB: faster than the next-best engine
charts.subtitle: Speed of ashalliants/ninfer-3090 divided by the fastest other engine we could run or find for each model on the same card. Above 1.0x means ours is faster. Decode is the geometric mean over the prompts in each model's chart.
charts.desc: Speed-up of ashalliants/ninfer-3090 over the next-best engine on one Tesla V100 32 GB. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B vs llama.cpp: 1.34x decode, 1.20x prefill. Qwen3.8-27B vs Lapilli: 1.21x decode, 1.38x prefill. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next vs Lapilli: 1.02x decode, prefill not compared. Inkling-2-Mini vs Strata's reported figures: 1.34x decode, 1.19x prefill with an 8192-token chunk (0.95x at the default chunk).

charts.title: Qwen3.8-27B on one Tesla V100 32 GB
charts.subtitle: ashalliants/ninfer-3090 against Lapilli (chris83-dev/lapilli-v100 f9b7dd09), both run on this card with the same prompts, greedy, 300 output tokens, warm. Both of our configurations are shown: each wins different prompts.
charts.desc: Qwen3.8-27B decode and prefill on one Tesla V100: ashalliants/ninfer-3090 with DFlash2 K7 and with MTP3 against Lapilli.

panels.title: Decode, one request (tok/s)
panels.note: Conversation (temperature 0.6) and JSON are Lapilli's basalt-bench fixtures (seed 7); the JSON prompt runs to about 7.2-7.6K output tokens.

panels.title: Prefill (tok/s)
panels.note: A fresh prompt each time, two repeats each (ours 951-958 at 4.2K).

panels.title: Decode at long context, MTP3 (tok/s)
panels.note: Decode after a prompt of that many tokens, build 3c6a616d with #608/#609, against master before them. Lapilli was not run at long context.

notes: Where we lose: our DFlash2 router configuration is slower than Lapilli on story (61.5 vs 69.0) and Chinese (41.4 vs 48.3); MTP3 wins those but is slower than Lapilli on code (110.2 vs 119.9) and JSON (126.1 vs 175.8). Use MTP3 for prose and non-English text, DFlash2 for code, thinking and structured output.
Quants differ: ours is the Qwen3.8-27B Q4/Q5 group-quant mix (19.0 GB), Lapilli runs its Qwen3.8-27B QUASAR NVFP4 pack (21.1 GB). A second Lapilli run agreed: story 69.3, code 123.0, thinking 97.2.

charts.subtitle: ashalliants/ninfer-3090 against Lapilli (f9b7dd09) on this card, same five prompts, greedy, a 150-token thinking budget. The 512-expert model's experts stream from host RAM over a PCIe Gen3 x4 link.

panels.title: Prefill (tok/s)
panels.note: No same-box Lapilli prefill figure. The two reported rows are derived by us from time to first token on another box (i9-10940X, 96 GB RAM), so they include request overheads.

rows.detail: 7,242-token prompt, IQ3_S, from an 8.7 s TTFT

rows.label: Strata (user nebod99)
rows.detail: same test, from a 22.6 s TTFT

notes: Close race: we lead Lapilli on all five prompts, by 0.2% (thinking) to 8% (French). Quants differ but sit in the same size class: ours is ISTA-DASLab's GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS repacked, Lapilli's is Unsloth's UD-IQ2_XS. With the router's flags ours reaches 129.6 on code.
Hosts with more RAM and a wider link report more: FNFL reports 106.8 tok/s (poetry, IQ3_XXS, 128 GB RAM, PCIe x8), above our story figure.

panels.note: llama.cpp is shown at its best mode for each prompt (MTP with 2 or 3 drafts, or DFlash with 7), named beside its bar. Our DFlash K7 was measured on code and JSON only.

panels.note: llama.cpp with a tuned batch (-ub 2048 -b 4096); at its default batch it reached 2,745 at 4.2K. The longest prompts differ: ours 40.2K tokens, llama.cpp 50K.

notes: Closest call: JSON, where llama.cpp's DFlash n7 (293) is within 4% of our MTP3 (302.9) and 8% behind our DFlash K7 (319.1). Our DFlash K7 is slower than our MTP3 on code (233.6 vs 253.7). Two requests at once: 197.5-200.4 tok/s in total (MTP3, #614).

notes: Reported figures are copied from pinned sources (docs/tesla-v100.md, "Methodology and sources") and were not re-run here; power limits are mostly not stated. Strata's card still carried "VERIFY before publishing" comments in its source. Strata's packs are smaller than ours: SQ-20 is 19.35 GB and SQ-10 10.47 GB, against our full Q8_K_XL at 23.9 GB (Strata reports SQ-20 matching the original on its own tests; SQ-10 drifts, perplexity +0.32). Smaller quants usually decode faster.
